'''Kinsey Amor Anderson''' (September 18, 1926 – June 11, 2012) was professor emeritus of physics at the [[University of California at Berkeley]] (UCB) and an internationally known pioneer of [[space physics]] during the early years of rocket, balloon, and satellite exploration of the [[upper atmosphere]], [[cosmic rays]], solar-terrestrial environment, and [[solar physics]].<ref>[http://newscenter.berkeley.edu/2012/06/29/pioneering-space-physicist-kinsey-anderson-has-died-at-85/ ''Pioneering space physicist Kinsey Anderson has died at 85''] : Robert Sanders, UC Berkeley press release, June 29, 2012.</ref><ref>[http://www.sfgate.com/science/article/Kinsey-Anderson-UC-Berkeley-space-physicist-dies-3687276.php ''Kinsey Anderson, UC Berkeley space physicist, dies''] : David Perlman. San Francisco Chronicle July 5, 2012</ref>

Anderson was born in [[Preston, Minnesota]]. He was the son of Malvin Anderson and Allene (Michener) Anderson. He received his BA in physics from [[Carleton College]] in 1949, his PhD in physics from the [[University of Minnesota]]  under [[John R. Winckler|Prof. John Winckler]] in 1955, and joined the UC Berkeley physics department in 1960. He served in the [[U. S. Navy]]  in 1945-1946. Anderson was a [[Guggenheim Fellow]] in 1959-1960.<ref>{{cite web|url=  https://aas.org/obituaries/kinsey-anderson-1926-2012|title=  Kinsey A. Anderson (1926 - 2012)|publisher=  American Astronomical Society|accessdate=  May 15, 2016|archive-date=  June 16, 2016|archive-url=  https://web.archive.org/web/20160616164823/https://aas.org/obituaries/kinsey-anderson-1926-2012|url-status=  dead}}</ref>

During the following decade at UCB he and his students flew instruments on many of the early generation of space science missions, including the [[Interplanetary Monitoring Platform]]s (IMP) 1-6, [[Orbiting Geophysical Observatory|OGO]] 5, Explorer 33 and 35, and [[Apollo Program|Apollo 15 and 16]] lunar sub-satellites.  He was an author on about 200 scientific papers, and trained 24 graduate students at Berkeley.
He was director of the [[Space Sciences Laboratory]] (SSL) at UCB, and a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web
|url=  https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/kinsey-a-anderson-3zo4m1/
|title=  Kinsey A. Anderson | publisher=The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine  |access-date= May 15, 2016}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite web|url=   https://www.nasonline.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/anderson-kinsey.pdf|title=  Kinsey A. Anderson  
|publisher= National Academy of Sciences   Biographical Memoirs  |access-date= May 15, 2016}}</ref>
